title: Rapid risk anchors and negotiation notes
body:
Purpose: quick personal field notes for upcoming partner contract reviews — items to flag, suggested fallback language, and 1-2 line scripts for calls. Keep short; this is a working cheat sheet for fast redlines and on-the-fly asks.

High-level redline priorities (ranked quick):
- Safety / data controls (customer data, inference logs, retention, encryption) — tie to product modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- IP for outputs and derivatives (model output rights, customer ownership vs joint rights).
- Liability / indemnity ceilings and carveouts (data breaches, export controls, indemnity triggers).
- SLA & ops (SLOs, throughput/latency metrics, credits, rollback triggers, failover behaviors).
- Subprocessors & auditability (right to audit, subprocessors list, SOC2 evidence cadence).

Notes-to-self: specific clauses worth zeroing in on
- Model output IP: vendor is pushing broad license back to themselves — ask for express customer ownership of "Customer Input and Output" and a narrow service license to vendor for operational use (monitoring/quality). Sample ask: "Customer retains all rights in Customer Input and Generated Output. Provider is granted a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use Outputs solely to perform the Service and to improve Service operations, subject to anonymization and aggregation requirements."

- Data retention & inference logs: we must not let vendor keep raw inputs for >30 days without explicit consent. For hosted plan keep retention <=30d by default, with opt-in for longer retention and clear deletion APIs. If vendor insists, require encryption-at-rest + KMS control for private deployments.

- Security incident notification: require 72-hour notification for incidents affecting customer data, with required remediation plan and post-mortem within 30 days. If incident causes data exfiltration, immediate right to suspend service + preserve evidence.

- Liability cap: typical vendor cap = fees paid in preceding 12 months. Push for higher multiple (x2-3) or carveouts for catastrophic breaches and IP indemnity. At minimum, carveout unlimited liability for willful misconduct, gross negligence, and breaches of data protection obligations.

- Indemnity scope: avoid unilateral IP indemnity from customer unless very narrow. Vendor should indemnify for third-party claims that the Service infringes IP, and for security/data breach claims stemming from vendor negligence.

- Export controls & sanctions: vendor must not host or process data in sanctioned jurisdictions; include right to terminate if export/regulatory risk arises. Require vendor compliance covenant and immediate notification if OFAC or similar lists impact processing.

- Subprocessors: require list of approved subprocessors and 30 days notice before adding new ones. Right to object and alternative (in case of objection, vendor must offer stopgap or permit termination without penalty).

- Audit / compliance evidence: SOC2 Type 2 report and penetration test report required annually for hosted offering; for Dedicated/Private deployments, require on-demand audit access or SOC2 + ISO27001. If they say "available on request" — specify time window for delivery (10 business days).

- Escrow & continuity: for critical deployments, push for source/operational escrow or business continuity plan. Minimum: code escrow trigger = prolonged vendor insolvency or failure to meet SLAs for X days.

- SLA specifics to pin down:
  - Latency SLOs: median vs p95 vs p99 — clients want p95 guarantees for interactive features. If vendor offers only median, push for p95 target and credits tied to p99.
  - Throughput/Concurrency: define how spikes are handled — automatic burst policies vs throttling; require documented throttling behavior and notification.
  - Credits: cap on credits and how they're calculated — avoid vendor capping credits at a token-level that is meaningless; ask for formula and materiality thresholds.

Negotiation scripts (one-liners for calls)
- "We can accept a limited license back to you for operation and quality improvement only, but we need clear anonymization controls and opt-out for retention beyond 30 days."
- "If a security event exposes customer data, we need to be notified within 72 hours and given evidence to support remediation steps."
- "Our exposure on user data and IP needs to be capped — we can discuss a fee-based uplift for higher liability limits but we need core carveouts for data breaches and willful misconduct."

Fallback/concession ladder (fast):
- Ideal: full Customer ownership of outputs + strong retention limits + SOC2 + higher liability multiple.
- Middle: customer ownership + vendor limited operational license + 90-day retention on logs + SOC2 within 30 days of request + liability cap = 12 months fees x2.
- Minimal acceptable: shared license for non-commercial improvement + 180-day retention + SOC2 upon request (10 business days) + standard cap (12 months fees) but with explicit carveouts for data breach and willful misconduct.

Sample redline snippets (quick grab)
- "Customer Data" definition must explicitly include "Customer Input" and "Customer Generated Output".
- "Provider may not use Customer Input or Generated Output for training models or for product improvement without Customer's prior written consent." (if they push back, change to "anonymized aggregation" with right to opt-out).
- Incident notification: "Provider shall notify Customer within seventy-two (72) hours of becoming aware of any Security Incident affecting Customer Data and shall provide all reasonable cooperation and assistance to mitigate harm."

Open Qs / escalate items
- How does vendor define "anonymized"? (ask for technique-level defs or examples)
- Will vendor accept KMS-control for Dedicated vs Hosted? If not, escalate to infra/product.
- Any pre-existing third-party model providers used by vendor (open-source vs licensed) — require disclosure and IP-risk assessment.

Redline play for special cases (Private / On-prem)
- Require stronger audit rights and on-site inspection rights for on-prem/appliance models.
- Demand indemnity substitution when vendor manages keys or has root access.

Personal heuristics when on calls
- Start with data/retention and output ownership — if you get those you protect 80% of risk.
- Use short, concrete examples ("If our customer uploads PHI, who owns the output? who can see logs? how long are they kept?")
- Keep the negotiation transactional: propose 1-2 concrete language swaps per call rather than philosophical debate.

Quick checklist before sending redline
- Ensure "Output" term exists and is defined.
- Ensure deletion API / process is described.
- Confirm incident timelines and evidence obligations.
- Confirm subprocessors list & notice period.
- Add SOC2 / pen test delivery timeframe.

End notes / reminders to self
- For strategic customers consider standalone Addendum for security + escrow.
- Keep evidence of negotiation (emails, Slack) if vendor refuses carveouts — helps in escalation to sales/finance.
- Sync with product (Theo) on feasibility of retention asks for hosted tier — don't over-push impossible asks without technical alignment.

— LM (quick field notes)
